correctness.rationale: For any characteristic p the differential f g′-g f′ has leading coefficient (j-r)f_r g_j, forcing centralizer formulas. Decomposing tuples by minimum valuation gives disjoint stratum counts: unit-leading q^(p-1)(q^m-1), low-positive q^(p-2r+(r-1)m)(q^m-1) via a uniquely normalized quotient line modulo H_(p-r+1), and high-positive (q^m-1)q^((p-r-1)m) because H_r is abelian. Zero tuple and m=0 boundaries included. The checker independently enumerates kernels by finite-field elimination and computes triple counts by intersections for q=2,4,3,9,5.

originality.rationale: Yao–Chang (2013) Lemma 2.3 establishes centralizer forms but does not state an all-arity finite-field point count; the new assertion is an explicit disjoint count by the minimum valuation and uniquely normalized quotient line, for every characteristic, every arity and each filtered subalgebra. Yao–Chang (2018) and Yao–Zhang (2021) discuss geometric commuting varieties, with the latter claiming component dimensions; the accessible abstracts do not state finite-field counts and component geometry by itself cannot yield these exact arithmetic totals. Relevant private earlier claims concerned derivation centralizer nullity and only restricted-nilpotent tuples at characteristic five; neither supplies the unrestricted uniform all-primes/all-arities count. A high historical overlap risk remains because the full 2018 and 2021 texts were inaccessible.

value.rationale: Exact F_q point counts of unrestricted commuting varieties at every arity are a natural arithmetic refinement of established geometric commuting-variety classifications of simple modular Witt Lie algebras. Formula resolves overlap among centralizers using unique normalized quotient directions and applies uniformly to every characteristic and each filtered positive-degree subalgebra. It provides exact commuting probabilities, all-arity growth and full arithmetic counts not determined by component counts or dimensions alone; no claim of new centralizer theory is made.
